I thought maybe that room was worth a billion dollars or something outrageous because there was like 20 paintings in there, you know. So priceless.
cues.zh: 纽约的一个房间里。我不记得是哪个博物馆了，但那是一个满是文艺复兴艺术的房间，你知道，都是伟大的画家，最伟大的画家。我想那个房间大概值十亿美元或者什么离谱的数目，因为里面有大概20幅画，你知道。所以是无价的。

cues.en: And the first thing is, well, why are those paintings worth so much? And why is there a museum in the biggest city in the world devoted to them? And why do people from all over the world come and look at them? What the hell are those people doing? One of them was of the assumption of Mary. You know, beautifully painted, absolutely
cues.zh: 首先，为什么这些画那么值钱？为什么世界上最大的城市里有一座博物馆专门收藏它们？为什么世界各地的人都来观赏它们？这些人到底在干什么？其中一幅画是《圣母升天》。你知道，画得美轮美奂，绝对

cues.en: glowing
cues.zh: 光彩夺目

cues.en: work of art and there's like 20 people standing in front of it looking at it. You think, what are those people up to?
cues.zh: 的艺术作品，却有大约20个人站在它面前盯着看。你会想，这些人在干什么呢？

cues.en: You know, they don't know. Why did they make a pilgrimage to New York to come and look at that painting? It's not like they know. Why is it worth so much? I know there's a status element to it too, but that begs the question, why did those items become such high status items? What is it about them that's so absolutely remarkable?
cues.zh: 你知道，他们其实也不懂。为什么他们要千里迢迢去纽约看那幅画？又不是因为他们真懂。为什么它那么值钱？我知道这里面也有身份地位的成分，但这就引出了一个问题：为什么这些东西会成为如此高身份的象征？它们究竟有什么如此非凡之处？

cues.en: Well, we're strange creatures.
cues.zh: 嗯，我们是奇怪的生物。

cues.en: So I was trying to figure out in part, well, where did the information that's in the dream come from? Because it has to come from somewhere, and you could think about it as a revelation.
cues.zh: 所以我部分是想弄清楚，梦里那些信息到底是从哪来的？因为它总得有个来源，而你可以把它看作一种启示。

cues.en: You know? Because it's it's like it springs out of the void and it's new knowledge and it's a revelation. You didn't produce it, it just appears.
cues.zh: 你知道吗？因为它就像从虚无中蹦出来，是全新的知识，是一种启示。不是你生产出来的，它就是出现了。

cues.en: But that's... See, one of the things I wanna do with this series is, like, I am scientifically minded and I'm quite a rational person, and I like to have an explanation for things that's rational
cues.zh: 但那……你看，我做这个系列想做的一件事就是，我是有科学思维的，我是个相当理性的人，我喜欢在寻求任何其他解释之前，先给事物一个理性的

cues.en: and empirical before I look for any other kind of explanation.
cues.zh: 和基于经验的解释。

cues.en: And I don't want to say that everything that's associated with divinity can be reduced in some manner to biology or to an evolutionary history or anything like that. But insofar
cues.zh: 我并不想说，所有与神性相关的事物都能以某种方式还原为生物学或进化史之类的东西。但就

cues.en: as it's possible to do that reduction, I'm going to do that.
cues.zh: 尽可能做到这种还原而言，我会去做。

cues.en: And I'm going to leave the other phenomena floating in the air because they can't be pinned down.
cues.zh: 而其他现象我会让它们悬在空中，因为它们无法被确定下来。

cues.en: In that category, I would put the category of mystical or religious experience, which we don't understand at all.
cues.zh: 在这一类里，我会放入神秘或宗教体验的范畴，那是我们完全无法理解的。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: artists observe one another.
cues.zh: 艺术家们互相观察。

cues.en: They observe people and they represent what they see. And they transmit the message of what they see to us and they teach us to see. And we don't necessarily know what it is that we're learning from them. But we're learning something, or at least we're acting like we're learning something. We go to movies, we watch stories,
cues.zh: 他们观察人们，并表现他们所看到的。他们把看到的讯息传递给我们，教我们如何去观察。我们未必知道自己从他们那里学到了什么。但我们确实在学，或者至少在表现得像是在学。我们去看电影，我们看故事，

cues.en: we
cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: immerse ourselves in fiction constantly. That's an artistic production.
cues.zh: 不断让自己沉浸在虚构作品中。那是一种艺术创作。

cues.en: And for many people, the world of the arts is a living world. And that's particularly true if you're a creative person. And it's the creative artistic people that do move the knowledge of humanity forward. And they do that with their artistic productions first. They're on the edge. The dancers do that, and the poets do that, and the visual artists do that and the musicians do that and we're not sure what they're doing. We're not sure what musicians are doing. What the hell are they doing? Why do you like music?
cues.zh: 对很多人来说，艺术的世界是一个鲜活的世界。如果你是创作者，就更是如此。正是富有创造力的艺术工作者推动着人类知识向前发展。他们首先通过自己的艺术创作做到这一点。他们处在最前沿。舞者如此，诗人如此，视觉艺术家如此，音乐家也如此，而我们并不确定他们在做什么。我们不确定音乐家在做什么。他们到底在干什么？你为什么喜欢音乐？

cues.en: You know, it gives you a deep intimation of the significance of things.
cues.zh: 你知道，它会让你深刻感受到事物的意义。

cues.en: And then no one questions it. You go to a concert, you're thrilled, it's a quasi religious experience, particularly if the people really get themselves together and get the crowd moving. You know, there's something incredibly intense about it but it makes no sense whatsoever.
cues.zh: 然后没人质疑它。你去听音乐会，你激动不已，那是一种近乎宗教般的体验，尤其是当人们真正齐心合力、带动全场的时候。你知道，那里面有种极其强烈的力量，但它根本说不通。

cues.en: It's not an easy thing to understand.
cues.zh: 这不是件容易理解的事。

cues.en: Music is deeply patterned,
cues.zh: 音乐是深具模式的，

cues.en: patterned
cues.zh: 有模式的

cues.en: in layers, and I think that has something to do with it because reality
cues.zh: 分层地富有模式，我觉得这跟它有几分关系，因为现实

cues.en: is patterned and deeply patterned in layers. And so I think music is representing reality in some fundamental way and that we get into the sway of that and sort of participate
cues.zh: 是有模式的，并且深具分层模式。所以我认为音乐在某种程度上以某种根本的方式再现了现实，而我们进入那种律动之中，某种程度上参与

cues.en: in being and that's part of what makes it such an uplifting experience. But we don't really know that's what we're doing. We just go do it.
cues.zh: 到存在之中，这正是它成为如此令人振奋的体验的部分原因。但我们并不真正知道自己在这么做。我们只是去做而已。

cues.en: And it's nourishing for people, right? Young
cues.zh: 它对人有滋养作用，对吧？年轻人

cues.en: people in particular,
cues.zh: 特别是人们，

cues.en: lots of them live for music. It's where they derive all their meaning, their cultural identity. Everything that's nourishing comes from their affiliation with their music. It is part of their cultural identity.
cues.zh: 很多人的生活离不开音乐。他们从音乐中获得全部意义和文化认同。一切滋养都来自他们与音乐的联结。音乐是他们文化认同的一部分。

cues.en: So that's an amazing thing.
cues.zh: 这太棒了。

cues.en: The question still remains, where does the information in dreams come from?
cues.zh: 问题依然存在：梦中的信息究竟来自何处？

cues.en: And I think
cues.zh: 我觉得

cues.en: where it comes from is that we watch
cues.zh: 它来源于我们观察到的

cues.en: the patterns that everyone
cues.zh: 大家都用的那些模式

cues.en: acts out. We've
cues.zh: 表现出来。我们已经

cues.en: that forever and we've got some representations
cues.zh: 这是永久的，我们有一些表示形式

cues.en: of those patterns. That's part of our cultural history. That's what's embedded in stories, in fictional accounts of the story between good and evil, the bad guy and the good guy, and the romance. You know, these are these are canonical patterns of being for people, and and they deeply affect us because they represent what it is that we will act out in the world. And then we flesh that out with the individual information we have about ourselves and other people. And so, it's like there's a there's waves
cues.zh: 这些模式中的一部分，是我们文化历史的一部分。它嵌入在故事里，嵌入在善与恶、坏人与好人之间，以及爱情故事中。这些是人们存在的经典模式，深深影响着我们，因为它们代表了我们在世界上将会演绎的东西。然后我们用关于自己和他人的个体信息去充实它。所以，就像有波浪一样

cues.en: of behavioral
cues.zh: 行为方面的

cues.en: patterns that manifest themselves in the crowd across time. Great dramas are played on the crowd across time. And the artists watch that and they get intimations of what that is, and they write it down and they tell us. And then we're a little clearer about what we're up to. You know, like a great dramatist like Shakespeare, let's say, know that what he wrote is fiction, and then we say, well, fiction isn't true.
cues.zh: 在时间的长河里，人群中显现出各种模式。伟大的戏剧在时间的长河中于人群里上演。艺术家们观察这些，获得对本质的暗示，他们记录下来并告诉我们。于是我们对自己的所为有了更清晰的认识。你知道，就像伟大的剧作家莎士比亚，他知道自己写的是虚构作品，然后我们说，虚构并非真实。

cues.en: But then you think, well, wait a minute. Maybe it's true like numbers are true.
cues.zh: 但接着你会想，等等。也许它就像数字一样，是真的。

cues.en: You know, numbers are an abstraction from the underlying reality, but no one in their right mind would really think numbers aren't true. You could even make a case that the numbers are more real than the things that they represent, right? Because the abstraction is so insanely
cues.zh: 你知道，数字是对底层现实的抽象，但任何心智正常的人都不会真的认为数字不真实。你甚至可以论证，数字比它们所代表的事物更真实，对吧？因为这种抽象极其

cues.en: powerful.
cues.zh: 强大。

cues.en: Once you have mathematics,
cues.zh: 一旦你掌握了数学，

cues.en: you're just deadly.
cues.zh: 你就所向披靡了。

cues.en: You can move the world with mathematics.
cues.zh: 你可以用数学改变世界。

cues.en: And so it's not obvious that the abstraction is less real than the
cues.zh: 所以，抽象并不显然比

cues.en: more concrete reality.
cues.zh: 更具体的现实更不真实。

cues.en: And you take a work of fiction like Hamlet and you think, well, is that... It's
cues.zh: 你拿《哈姆雷特》这样的虚构作品来看，你会想，这是……它

cues.en: not true because it's fiction. But then you think, wait a minute. What kind of explanation is that? Maybe it's more true than nonfiction.
cues.zh: 不是真的，因为它是虚构的。但接着你会想，等等。那算是什么解释？也许它比非虚构还要真实。

cues.en: Because it takes what... The story that needs to be told about you and the story that needs to be told about you and you and you and you and abstracts that out and says, look, here's something that's a key part of the human experience
cues.zh: 因为它提取了……关于你的故事，以及关于你、你、你、你的故事，把这一切抽象出来，说，看，这是人类经验的一个关键部分

cues.en: as such.
cues.zh: 本身。

cues.en: Right? So it's an abstraction from this underlying
cues.zh: 对吧？所以它是从这底下

cues.en: noisy
cues.zh: 嘈杂的

cues.en: substrate.
cues.zh: 基底中抽象出来的。

cues.en: And people are affected by it because they see that the thing that's represented is part of the pattern of their being. That's the right way to think about it. And then, with these old stories, these ancient stories, it seems to me like that process has been occurring for thousands of years. It's like, we watched ourselves and we extracted out some stories. We imitated each other and we represented that in drama, and then we distilled the drama and we got a representation
cues.zh: 人们受它影响，因为他们看到所表现的东西是他们存在模式的一部分。这才是正确的理解方式。然后，借着这些古老的故事，在我看来，这个过程似乎已经持续了几千年。就像是，我们观察自己，提炼出了一些故事。我们互相模仿，把它表现在戏剧里，然后我们提炼戏剧，得到了一种

cues.en: of the distillation. And then we did it again. And at the end of that process, it took God only knows how long.
cues.zh: 提炼之物的再现。然后我们又做了一遍。而在这个过程的尽头，花了天知道多久的时间。

cues.en: I think some of these stories
cues.zh: 我认为其中一些故事

cues.en: they've traced fairy tales back ten thousand years, some fairy tales, in relatively unchanged form.
cues.zh: 他们追溯童话到一万年前，一些童话，形态相对未变。

cues.en: And it certainly seems to me that the archaeological
cues.zh: 在我看来，考古

cues.en: evidence, for example, suggests that the really old stories that
cues.zh: 证据，例如，表明那些真正古老的故事，

cues.en: the Bible begins with are at least that old and likely embedded in a prehistory that's far older than that. You might think, well,
cues.zh: 《圣经》开篇的那些，至少有那么古老，很可能根植于更古老的史前时期。你可能想，好吧，

cues.en: how can you be so sure? The answer to that in part is that cultures that don't change,
cues.zh: 你怎么能这么确定？部分答案在于那些不变的文 化，

cues.en: like the ancient cultures, right? They didn't change as fast as us. They stay the same.
cues.zh: 像古代文化，对吧？它们不像我们变化那么快。它们保持不变。

cues.en: That's the answer.
cues.zh: 这就是答案。

cues.en: So they keep their information moving generation to generation. That's how they stay the same.
cues.zh: 这样信息就能一代代传下去。它们也正是借此保持不变。

cues.en: And so we know, again, in the archaeological record, there are records of rituals that have remained relatively unbroken for up to twenty thousand years. It was discovered in caves in Japan that were set up for a particular kind of bear worship that was also characteristic of Western Europe. So these things can last for very long periods of time.
cues.zh: 所以我们在考古记录中再次看到，有些仪式相对未曾中断地延续了长达两万年。在日本的一些洞穴里就曾发现过，这些洞穴是为某种特定的熊崇拜而布置的，而这种崇拜在西欧也有。所以这些东西能持续非常长的时间。

cues.en: We're watching each other
cues.zh: 我们一直在互相观察

cues.en: act in the world.
cues.zh: 在世界上行动。

cues.en: And then the question is, well, how long have we been watching each other? And the answer to that, in some sense, is, well, as long as there's been creatures with nervous systems.
cues.zh: 那么问题来了，我们互相观察了多久？某种意义上，答案是，只要有神经系统生物存在，我们就一直在观察。

cues.en: And that's a long time, you know, that's some hundreds of millions of years, perhaps longer than that. We've been watching each other, trying to figure out what we're up to across that entire span of time. Some of that knowledge is built right into our bodies, which is why we can dance with each other, for example. Right? Because understanding isn't just something
cues.zh: 那是很长的时间，你知道，有几亿年，也许更长。在这整段时间里，我们一直在互相观察，试图弄明白对方在做什么。有些知识直接内置在我们身体里，这就是为什么我们能一起跳舞。对吧？因为理解不只是

cues.en: that you have as an abstraction, it's something that you act out.
cues.zh: 一种抽象的东西，它是你付诸行动的东西。

cues.en: That's what children are doing when they're learning to rough and tumble play, is they're learning to integrate their body with the body of someone else in a harmonious way, learning to cooperate and compete. And that's all instantiated
cues.zh: 孩子们在学习打闹玩耍时，正是在学习如何以和谐的方式将自己的身体与他人的身体协调起来，学习合作与竞争。而这一切都直接

cues.en: right into their body. It's not abstract knowledge. They don't know that they're doing that. They're just doing it. And so we can even use our body as a representational
cues.zh: 体现在他们的身体中。这不是抽象的知识。他们并不知道自己在这么做。他们只是在做。所以我们甚至可以把身体当作一个表征

cues.en: platform.
cues.zh: 平台。

cues.en: So we've been studying each other for a long time, abstracting
cues.zh: 我们互相研究很久了，一直在抽象

cues.en: out what is it that we're up to. And that's
cues.zh: 我们到底在做什么。那也就是

cues.en: what is it we're up to? What should we be up to? That's even a more fundamental question.
cues.zh: 我们到底在做什么？我们应该做什么？这甚至是更根本的问题。

cues.en: If you're going to live in the world and you're going to do it properly,
cues.zh: 如果你要活在这个世界上，而且想活得恰当，

cues.en: what does properly mean and how is it that you might go about that? Well, it's the right question. Right? It's what everyone wants to know. How do you live in the world? Not what is the world made of? It's not the same question. How do you live in the world? It's the eternal question of human beings. And I guess we're the only species that has ever really asked that question because all the other animals, they just go and do whatever they do.
cues.zh: 恰当意味着什么，你又该如何做到？嗯，这才是正确的问题。对吧？这是每个人都想知道的。你如何在这个世界上生活？而不是世界由什么构成？这不是同一个问题。你如何在这个世界上生活？这是人类永恒的问题。我猜我们是唯一真正问过这个问题的物种，因为其他动物只是去做它们该做的事。

cues.en: Not us.
cues.zh: 不是我们。

cues.en: It's a question for us. We've had to... We have to become aware of it. We have to be able to speak it. God only knows why.
cues.zh: 这是我们要面对的问题。我们不得不……我们必须意识到它。我们必须能够把它说出来。天知道为什么。

cues.en: But that seems to be the situation.
cues.zh: 但情况似乎就是这样。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: we act. That acting is shaped by the world, that acting is shaped by society into something that we don't understand, but that we can model.
cues.zh: 我们行动。行动被世界塑造，行动被社会塑造成我们无法理解的东西，但我们可以对它建模。

cues.en: That we can model. We model it in our stories. We model it with our bodies.
cues.zh: 我们可以建模。我们在故事中建模。我们用身体建模。

cues.en: And that's where the dream gets its information.
cues.zh: 梦想正是从这里获取信息。

cues.en: The dream is part of the process that's watching everything
cues.zh: 梦是那个观照一切的过程的一部分

cues.en: and then trying to formulate it and trying to say... Well, trying to get the signal out from the noise and to portray it in dramatic form because a dream is little drama. And then you get the chance to talk about what that dream is.
cues.zh: 然后试着把它组织出来，试着说……试着从噪声中提取信号，并以戏剧化的形式呈现出来，因为梦就是小小的戏剧。然后你才有机会谈论那个梦到底是什么。

cues.en: And then you have something
cues.zh: 然后你就有了某种东西

cues.en: like articulated knowledge at that point.
cues.zh: 在那一刻就像是清晰表达出来的知识。

cues.en: And so the Bible, I would say,
cues.zh: 所以圣经，我会说，

cues.en: it exists
cues.zh: 它存在于

cues.en: in that space that's half into the dream and half into articulated knowledge. It's something like that. And going into it to find out what the stories are about
cues.zh: 那个半在梦中、半在清晰表达的知识中的空间里。大概就是这样。而深入其中去了解那些故事讲的是什么

cues.en: can
cues.zh: 能够

cues.en: what can what it can aid our self understanding.
cues.zh: 能够帮助我们的自我理解。

cues.en: And then the other issue is that if
cues.zh: 然后另一个问题是，如果

cues.en: Nietzsche was correct and if Dostoevsky
cues.zh: 尼采是对的，如果陀思妥耶夫斯基

cues.en: or Jung was correct and Dostoevsky as well,
cues.zh: 或者荣格是对的，陀思妥耶夫斯基也是对的，

cues.en: without the cornerstone
cues.zh: 没有那块基石

cues.en: that that understanding provides,
cues.zh: 那种理解所提供的基石，

cues.en: we're lost.
cues.zh: 我们就迷失了。

cues.en: And that's not good because then we're susceptible
cues.zh: 这可不妙，因为那样我们就容易

cues.en: to psychic pathology.
cues.zh: 患上精神病理。

cues.en: That's psychological
cues.zh: 那是心理

cues.en: pathology.
cues.zh: 病理。

cues.en: You know, the people who are
cues.zh: 你知道，那些

cues.en: adamant
cues.zh: 坚决

cues.en: anti religious
cues.zh: 反宗教的

cues.en: thinkers
cues.zh: 思想家

cues.en: seem to believe that if we abandoned

cues.zh: 你看。

cues.en: You take a text, you can interpret it a variety of ways, but that's not right. This is where the post modernists went wrong because
cues.zh: 拿一段文本，你可以用各种方式解读，但那样不对。这就是后现代主义者出错的地方，因为

cues.en: what you're looking for in a text, and in the world for that matter, is
cues.zh: 你在文本中寻找的，推而广之在世界上寻找的，是

cues.en: sufficient order and direction.
cues.zh: 足够的秩序和方向。

cues.en: So then we have to think, well, what does sufficient order and direction mean? Well, you don't wanna suffer so much that your life is unbearable.
cues.zh: 于是我们得想想，足够的秩序和方向到底是什么意思？嗯，你不想痛苦到生活难以忍受的地步。

cues.en: Right? That just seems self evident. Pain
cues.zh: 对吧？这似乎不言自明。痛苦

cues.en: argues for itself.
cues.zh: 本身就说明了一切。

cues.en: I think of pain as the fundamental reality because no one disputes it. Right? I mean, even if you say that you don't believe in pain, it doesn't help when you're in pain. You still believe in it. Right? It's it's it's... You can't
cues.zh: 我把痛苦看作根本现实，因为没人能否认它。对吧？我是说，就算你说自己不相信痛苦，当你真的痛苦时也没用。你还是会相信它。对吧？这这这……你没法

cues.en: pry it up with logic and rationality. It just stands forth as what the fundament of existence. And that's actually quite useful to know. Say, well you don't want any more of that than is absolutely necessary.
cues.zh: 用逻辑和理性把它撬开。它就是作为存在的根基赫然矗立。知道这一点其实很有用。就是说，除了绝对必要，你不会想要更多这种东西。

cues.en: And I think that's self evident. And then you say, wait a minute, it's more complicated than that.
cues.zh: 我觉得这是不言自明的。然后你说，等等，事情比这更复杂。

cues.en: You don't want any more of that that's necessary today,
cues.zh: 你今天不想要任何超出必要范围的东西，

cues.en: but also not tomorrow and not next week and not next month and not next year. So however you act now,
cues.zh: 明天也不要，下周也不要，下个月也不要，明年也不要。所以无论你现在怎么行动，

cues.en: better not compromise how you're going to be in a year, because that would just be counterproductive.
cues.zh: 最好别损害你一年后的状态，因为那只会适得其反。

cues.en: That's part of the problem with short term pleasures, right? It's like,
cues.zh: 这就是短期愉悦的部分问题所在，对吧？就像，

cues.en: act in haste, repent at leisure. Everyone knows exactly what that means. So you have to act in a way that works now and tomorrow and next week and next month and so forth. And so you have to take your future self into account.
cues.zh: 欲速则不达，事后徒伤悲。每个人都清楚那是什么意思。所以你得采取一种现在行得通、明天行得通、下周行得通、下个月也行得通的方式行动，以此类推。因此你必须把未来的自己考虑进去。

cues.en: And human beings can do that. And taking your future self into account isn't much different than taking other people into account.
cues.zh: 人类也能做到这点。而把未来的自己纳入考量，跟把其他人纳入考量并没有太大区别。

cues.en: Right? Because I remember there's this Simpson episode
cues.zh: 对吧？因为我记得《辛普森一家》有这么一集

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: Homer downs a quart of mayonnaise and vodka.
cues.zh: Homer 灌下一夸脱蛋黄酱加伏特加。

cues.en: And he says...
cues.zh: 他说……

cues.en: Someone... Marge says, you know, you shouldn't really do that. And Homer says, that's a problem for future Homer. I'm sure glad I'm not that guy.
cues.zh: 有人……Marge 说，你不该这么干的。Homer 说，那是未来 Homer 的问题。我真庆幸我不是那家伙。

cues.en: And so ridiculously comical, you know. But but,
cues.zh: 真是荒唐得可笑。不过不过，

cues.en: okay, but you see, we have to grapple with that. And so the you that's out there in the future is sort of like another person. And so figuring out how to conduct yourself properly in relationship to your future self isn't much different than figuring out how to conduct yourself in relationship to other people. But then we could expand the constraints.
cues.zh: 好吧，但你瞧，我们得应对这个问题。所以未来那个你，某种程度上就像另一个人。因此，想清楚如何恰当地处理与未来自己的关系，跟想清楚如何处理与他人的关系并没有太大区别。但接着我们还能扩展这些约束。

cues.en: Not only does the interpretation that you extract
cues.zh: 你提取出的解释不仅

cues.en: have to protect you from suffering and give you an aim, but it has to do it in a way that's iterable,
cues.zh: 要能保护你免于痛苦、给你一个目标，还得以可迭代的方式做到这一点，

cues.en: so it works across time. And then it has to work in the presence of other people, so that you can cooperate with them and compete with them in a way that doesn't make you suffer more. And people are...
cues.zh: 这样它才能跨越时间起作用。然后它还必须在有他人存在的情况下奏效，让你能与人合作、与人竞争，又不至于让自己更痛苦。而人们……

cues.en: They're not that tolerant.
cues.zh: 他们可没那么宽容。

cues.en: You know, mean, they have choices. They don't have to hang around with you. They can hang around with any one of these other primates. And so if you don't act properly, at least within certain boundaries, it's like, you're just
cues.zh: 你知道，他们挺刻薄的，他们是有选择的。他们没必要跟你待在一起，他们可以跟其他任何一只灵长类动物待在一起。所以如果你表现得不得体，至少在某些界限之内不得体，那你就只会

cues.en: cast aside.
cues.zh: 被抛到一边。

cues.en: And so people are broadcasting information at you all the time about how you need to interpret the world so they can tolerate being around you. And you need that because socially isolated, you're insane and then you're dead. No one can tolerate being alone for any length of time. We can't maintain our own sanity without continual feedback from other people because it's too damn complicated.
cues.zh: 于是人们一直在向你传递信息，告诉你该如何解读这个世界，这样他们才能忍受与你相处。而你需要这些，因为一旦社交孤立，你就会精神失常，然后你就完了。没人能忍受长时间独处。没有他人持续的反馈，我们无法维持自己的理智，因为这实在太复杂了。

cues.en: So you're constrained by your own existence, and then you're constrained by the existence of other people. And then you're also constrained by the world. Know, if I read Hamlet and what I extract out of that is the idea that I should jump off a bridge, it's like it's... It puts my interpretation to an end rather quickly.
cues.zh: 所以你受限于自身的存在，接着又受限于他人的存在。然后你还受限于这个世界。你知道，如果我读《哈姆雷特》，从中得出的想法是我应该跳桥，那就像是……它很快就终结了我的解读。

cues.en: It doesn't seem to be optimally functional, let's say. And so an interpretation is constrained by the reality of the world. It's constrained by the reality of other people, and it's constrained by your reality across time. There's only a small number of interpretations
cues.zh: 它似乎并不是最优的功能性，这么说吧。所以一种解读会受到现实世界的约束。它受到他人现实的约束，也受到你跨越时间的自身现实的约束。只有少数几种解读

cues.en: that are gonna work in that tightly defined space.
cues.zh: 能在那个被严格定义的范围内行得通。

cues.en: And so that's part of the reason that the post modernists are wrong.
cues.zh: 所以这也是后现代主义者错误的部分原因。

cues.en: It's also part of the reason, by the way, that AI people who've been trying to make intelligent machines have had to put them in a body.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，这也是为什么那些一直试图制造智能机器的 AI 研究者，不得不把它们放进一个身体里的部分原因。

cues.en: It turns out that you just can't make something intelligent in some sense without it being embodied.
cues.zh: 事实证明，如果不在某种意义上有身体，你就无法造出智能的东西。

cues.en: And it's partly for the reasons that I just described. You need constraints on the system before...
cues.zh: 部分原因就是我刚才描述的那些。你需要对系统施加约束，然后才能……

cues.en: You need constraints on the system so that the system doesn't drown in an infinite sea of interpretation.
cues.zh: 你需要对系统施加约束，这样系统才不会淹没在无限的解读海洋中。

cues.en: It's something like that.
cues.zh: 大概就是这样。

cues.en: So that's the literary end of it. Moral.
cues.zh: 这就是文学层面的部分。道德。

cues.en: Well, morality for me is about action. And I'm an existentialist in some sense, and what that means is that I believe that what people believe to be true is what they act out, not what they say.
cues.zh: 对我来说，道德关乎行动。我在某种意义上是存在主义者，这意味着我相信人们真正相信为真的东西是他们付诸行动的东西，而不是他们嘴上说的东西。

cues.en: And so there's lots of definitions of truth. I mean, truth is a very expansive word, and you can think of objective truth.
cues.zh: 所以关于真相有很多定义。我是说，真相是个很宽泛的词，你可以想到客观真相。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: behavioral truth isn't the same as objective truth. What you should do isn't the same as what is.
cues.zh: 行为真相和客观真相不一样。你应该怎么做，和实际是什么，并不是一回事。

cues.en: As far as I can tell, people debate that. But I think the reason that that has to be the case is because... Think about it this way. You're standing in front of a field,
cues.zh: 据我所知，人们对此有争论。但我认为这必然如此，原因在于……这样想吧。你站在一片田野前，

cues.en: and you can see the field,
cues.zh: 你能看到这片田野，

cues.en: but the field doesn't tell you how to walk through it. There's an infinite number of ways you could walk through it. And so you can't extract out an inviolable
cues.zh: 但田野不会告诉你该怎么穿过它。你穿过它的方式有无数种。所以你无法从眼前的这一堆事实中，提取出一份不可违背的

cues.en: guide to how you should act from the array of facts that are in front of you. Cause there's just too many facts.
cues.zh: 关于你该如何行动的指南。因为事实实在太多了。

cues.en: And they don't have directionality.
cues.zh: 它们没有方向性。

cues.en: But you, you need to know. You need to know how not to suffer and you need to know what your aim is. And so you have to overlay that objective reality with some interpretive structure.
cues.zh: 但你，你需要知道。你需要知道如何避免受苦，你需要知道你的目标是什么。所以你必须用某种解释性结构来覆盖那个客观现实。

cues.en: And it's the nature of that interpretive structure that we're going to be aiming at hard. I've given you some hints about it already. We've extracted it in part from observations of our own behavior and other people's behavior.
cues.zh: 而正是那个解释性结构的本质，我们将要着力探究。我已经给了你一些关于它的提示。我们已经部分地从对自身行为和他人行为的观察中提取出了它。

cues.en: And we've extracted it in part by the nature of our embodiment that's been shaped over hundreds of millions of years.
cues.zh: 我们之所以能部分提取这些，是因为我们的具身本质历经数亿年塑造而成。

cues.en: But we see the infinite plane of facts and we impose
cues.zh: 但我们看到无边无际的事实平面，于是强加

cues.en: a moral interpretation on it. And the moral interpretation
cues.zh: 一种道德解读于其上。而这种道德解读

cues.en: is what to do about what is.
cues.zh: 就是针对现状该做什么。

cues.en: And that's associated both with security,
cues.zh: 这与安全感相关，

cues.en: because you just don't need too much complexity,
cues.zh: 因为你不需要太多复杂性，

cues.en: and also with aim. And so we're mobile creatures, right? We need to know where we're going. Because all we're ever concerned about, roughly speaking, is where we're going. That's what we need to know. Where are we going? What are we doing? And why?
cues.zh: 也与目标相关。我们是移动的生物，对吧？我们需要知道自己要去哪里。因为大致来说，我们关心的始终只是我们要去哪里。这就是我们需要知道的。我们要去哪？我们在做什么？为什么？

cues.en: And that's not the same question as what is the world made of objectively?
cues.zh: 这和“世界客观上讲由什么构成”不是同一个问题。

cues.en: It's a different question. It requires different answers.
cues.zh: 这是另一个问题，需要不同的答案。

cues.en: And so that's the domain of the moral as far as I'm concerned, is what are you aiming at?
cues.zh: 所以在我看来，道德的领域就是：你瞄准的是什么？

cues.en: And that's the question of the ultimate ideal in some sense. Even if you have trivial little fragmentary
cues.zh: 某种意义上，这就是终极理想的问题。哪怕你只有一些微不足道的、零碎的

cues.en: ideals,
cues.zh: 理想，

cues.en: there's something
cues.zh: 也有某种东西

cues.en: trying to emerge out of that that's
cues.zh: 试图从中浮现出来，变得更

cues.en: more coherent and more integrated
cues.zh: 连贯、更整合、

cues.en: and more applicable and more practical.
cues.zh: 更适用、更实际。

cues.en: And that's the other thing, is that,
cues.zh: 还有另一点，就是，

cues.en: you
cues.zh: 你

cues.en: you think about literature and you think about art and you think those aren't very tightly tied to the earth. They're imperial and airy and spiritual, and they don't seem practical, but I'm
cues.zh: 你想到文学，想到艺术，觉得它们和现实大地联系不紧密。它们高高在上、空灵、精神化，看上去不实用，但我

cues.en: a practical person.
cues.zh: 是个务实的人。

cues.en: And part of the reason that I want to assess
cues.zh: 我想从文学、美学和进化视角来评估

cues.en: these books from a literary and aesthetic and evolutionary perspective is to extract out something of value, something of real value, that's practical.
cues.zh: 这些书，部分原因是要提炼出有价值的东西，真正有价值、实用的东西。

cues.en: You know, something... Because one of the rules that I have when I'm lecturing
cues.zh: 你知道，那个……因为我讲课的时候有个原则

cues.en: is that I don't wanna tell anybody anything that they can't use.
cues.zh: 就是我不想告诉别人任何他们用不上的东西。

cues.en: Because I think of knowledge as a tool. It's it's something to implement in the world. We're tool using creatures, and our knowledge is tools.
cues.zh: 因为我把知识看作工具。它是可以在现实中落地实施的东西。我们是使用工具的动物，我们的知识就是工具。

cues.en: And we need tools to work in the world. We need tools to regulate our emotions and to make things better and to put an end to suffering to the degree that we can, and to live with ourselves properly, and to stand up properly.
cues.zh: 我们需要工具在这个世界上做事。我们需要工具来调节情绪，把事情做得更好，尽可能地终结痛苦，和自己好好相处，堂堂正正地站起来。

cues.en: And you need the tools to do that.
cues.zh: 你需要相应的工具来做到这一点。

cues.en: And so I don't wanna do anything in this lecture series that isn't practical.
cues.zh: 所以在这系列讲座里，我不想讲任何不实用的东西。

cues.en: You know, I want you to come away
cues.zh: 我希望你们听完之后

cues.en: having things put together in a way that you can immediately imply, not
cues.zh: 能把知识组织成可以立刻运用的形式，而不是

cues.en: interested in
cues.zh: 为了抽象而抽象，

cues.en: abstraction for the sake of abstraction.
cues.zh: 我对那种不感兴趣。

cues.en: Rational.
cues.zh: 要合理。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: it's got to make sense, you know. Because
cues.zh: 必须说得通。因为

cues.en: the more restrictions on your theory, the better.
cues.zh: 你的理论限制越多越好。

cues.en: And so I
cues.zh: 所以我

cues.en: want it all laid out causally so that
cues.zh: 想把一切按因果顺序讲清楚，让

cues.en: B follows A and B precedes C and in a way that's understandable and doesn't require a leap
cues.zh: B 跟在 A 后面，B 又在 C 前面，而且方式要易懂，不需要盲目跳步，

cues.en: any unnecessary leap of faith. You know, because that's another thing that I think interferes
cues.zh: 不需要任何不必要的信仰跳跃。因为我觉得这也是妨碍

cues.en: with our relationship
cues.zh: 我们与

cues.en: with a
cues.zh: 像《圣经》这样的

cues.en: collection of books like the Bible, is that you're called upon to believe things that no one can believe.
cues.zh: 书籍集建立关系的一个因素：你被要求去相信一些没人能相信的东西。

cues.en: That's no good because that's a form of lie as far as I can tell. Then you have to scrap the whole thing because in principle the whole thing's about truth. And if you have to start your pursuit of truth by swallowing a bunch of lies, then how in the world are you gonna get anywhere with that?
cues.zh: 这不行，因为据我所知，那是一种谎言。那你就得把整件事都抛弃，因为原则上整件事都是关于真相的。如果你一开始追求真相就得先吞下一堆谎言，那你怎么可能走得下去？

cues.en: And so,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: I don't want any uncertainty
cues.zh: 我不想在这个根基上留有任何不确定性，

cues.en: at the bottom of this, I don't want any more than I can get... Than I have to leave in it, because I can't get any farther than that. And so we... It's gonna make sense rationally.
cues.zh: 我不想留下超出我不得不留下的不确定性……因为再往前我也走不了了。所以我们要……这在理性上是说得通的。

cues.en: I want it... I don't want it to be
cues.zh: 我想让它……我不想让它

cues.en: pushing up against what we know to be scientifically untrue, even though science is in flux and that's somewhat of a dangerous parameter.
cues.zh: 去对抗我们已知科学上不成立的东西，尽管科学本身也在变动，这算是个有点危险的参数。

cues.en: If it isn't working with evolutionary
cues.zh: 比如说，如果它不符合进化

cues.en: theory, for example, then I think that it's not a good enough solution.
cues.zh: 理论，那我觉得这个方案就不够好。

cues.en: So...
cues.zh: 所以……

cues.en: And then finally, it's phenomenological.
cues.zh: 最后一点，它是现象学的。

cues.en: Modern people,
cues.zh: 现代人，

cues.en: you know, we think of reality
cues.zh: 你知道，我们把现实

cues.en: as objective.
cues.zh: 看作是客观的。

cues.en: And that's very powerful.
cues.zh: 这非常强大。

cues.en: But that isn't how we experience reality.
cues.zh: 但这并不是我们体验现实的方式。

cues.en: We have our domain of experience, you know, and this is a hard thing to
cues.zh: 我们有自己的经验领域，你知道，这件事很难

cues.en: get a grip on, even though it should be the most obvious thing. For the phenomenologists,
cues.zh: 把握，尽管它应该是最显而易见的事情。对于现象学家来说，

cues.en: everything that you experience is real.
cues.zh: 你所经历的一切都是真实的。

cues.en: And so they're interested in the structure of your subjective experience. And you say, well, you have subjective experience, and you have subjective experience, and so do you. And there's commonalities across all of those. Like, for example, you're likely to experience
cues.zh: 所以他们对你的主观经验结构感兴趣。你说，嗯，你有主观经验，你有主观经验，你也有。而所有这些之间都有共同点。比如说，你很可能体验到

cues.en: the same set of emotions. You know, we've been able to identify canonical emotions
cues.zh: 同一组情绪。你知道，我们已经能够识别出典型的情绪

cues.en: and canonical motivations.
cues.zh: 和典型的动机。

cues.en: Without that, we couldn't even communicate, because you wouldn't know what the other person
cues.zh: 没有这些，我们甚至无法沟通，因为你不知道对方

cues.en: was like. You'd have to explain infinitely. There's nothing you could take for granted, but you can. You know, phenomenology
cues.zh: 是什么样的人。你得无限地解释。没有什么能想当然，但其实你可以。你知道，现象学

cues.en: is the fact that in the center of my vision my hands are very clear, and then out in the periphery they disappear.
cues.zh: 就是这样一个事实：在我视野的中心，我的双手非常清晰，而在边缘处它们就消失了。

cues.en: And phenomenology
cues.zh: 而现象学

cues.en: is the way things smell and the way things taste and the fact that they matter. And so you could say in some sense that phenomenology
cues.zh: 就是事物闻起来的样子、尝起来的样子，以及它们有意义这件事。所以某种程度上你可以说，现象学

cues.en: is
cues.zh: 是

cues.en: the study of what matters rather than matter.
cues.zh: 对“要紧之事”而非“物质”的研究。

cues.en: And it's a given from the phenomenological
cues.zh: 从现象学的角度来说，这是理所当然的。

cues.en: perspective that things have meaning.
cues.zh: 从视角来看，事物是有意义的。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.zh: 跨越多个时期。他们得出结论的方式

cues.en: that is by looking at textual analysis, trying
cues.zh: 是通过文本分析，试图

cues.en: to see where there are chunks of the stories that have the same kind of style or the same reference. People argue about that because
cues.zh: 找出故事中哪些部分具有相同的风格或相同的引用。人们对此有争议，因为

cues.en: obviously it's difficult to recreate something ancient,
cues.zh: 显然很难重现古代的东西，

cues.en: but that's
cues.zh: 但这就是

cues.en: the basic idea. So it is an amalgam
cues.zh: 基本思路。所以它是

cues.en: of viewpoints
cues.zh: 关于这些初始问题的

cues.en: about these initial issues, and that's important to know. So it's like a collective
cues.zh: 各种观点的融合，这一点很重要。所以它就像一个集体的

cues.en: it's a collective story.
cues.zh: 它是一个集体故事。

cues.en: And...
cues.zh: 还有……

cues.en: Okay. Now to understand the first part of Genesis,
cues.zh: 好，要理解《创世记》的第一部分，

cues.en: I'm going to turn,
cues.zh: 我要转向，

cues.en: strangely enough,
cues.zh: 说来奇怪，

cues.en: to
cues.zh: 转向

cues.en: something that's actually part of the New Testament, and this is a central element of Christianity.
cues.zh: 《新约》里的内容，而这是基督教的核心要素。

cues.en: And it's a very strange idea, and it's gonna take a very long time to unpack. But the idea,
cues.zh: 这是个非常奇特的概念，要花很长时间才能讲清楚。但这个概念，

cues.en: this is what John said about Christ. He said, in the beginning was the word. And so that relates back to Genesis one. In the beginning was the word, and the word was with God, and the word was God.
cues.zh: 这就是约翰对基督的描述。他说，太初有道。这就和《创世记》第一章联系起来了。太初有道，道与神同在，道就是神。

cues.en: Some...
cues.zh: Some...

cues.en: Well, you know, three sentences like that take a lot of unpacking because none of that seems to make any sense whatsoever,
cues.zh: 你知道，像这样的三句话需要大量解读，因为那些内容似乎完全说不通，

cues.en: really. Right? In the beginning was the word,
cues.zh: 真的。对吧？太初有道，

cues.en: and the word was both with God, and the word was God.
cues.zh: 道与神同在，道就是神。

cues.en: So the first question might be, what in the world does that mean? In the beginning was the word. That's the logos, actually.
cues.zh: 所以第一个问题可能是，这到底是什么意思？太初有道。那其实就是logos。

cues.en: And the logos is embodied in the figure of Christ. So there's this idea in John that whatever Christ is, the son of God, is not only instantiated in history, say at a particular time and place, as carpenter
cues.zh: 而logos体现在基督这个形象中。所以在约翰福音里有这样一种观念：无论基督是什么，神的儿子，不仅被实例化在历史中，比如在某个特定时间和地点，作为一个木匠

cues.en: in some backwoods part of the world, but also something eternal
cues.zh: 在世界某个偏僻的地方，而且是某种永恒的东西

cues.en: that exists outside of time and space that was there right at the beginning. As far as I can tell, what that logos represents is something like modern people. It's something like what modern people refer to when they talk about consciousness.
cues.zh: 存在于时间和空间之外，从一开始就在那里。据我所知，那个logos所代表的，类似于现代人。类似于现代人在谈论意识时所指的是什么。

cues.en: It's something like that. It's more than that. It's like consciousness
cues.zh: 差不多是这样。但不止于此。这就像是意识

cues.en: and its capacity
cues.zh: 以及它的能力

cues.en: to be aware and its capacity to communicate.
cues.zh: 去感知的能力，还有沟通的能力。

cues.en: It's something like that. And there's an idea underneath that, which is that being, especially from a phenomenological
cues.zh: 差不多是这样。这背后有个理念，尤其是从现象学的

cues.en: perspective, so the being that is experienced, cannot exist without consciousness.
cues.zh: 视角来看，被体验的存在，离不开意识而存在。

cues.en: It's like consciousness shines a light on things to bring it into being. Because without consciousness,
cues.zh: 就像是意识照亮事物，使之得以存在。因为没有意识，

cues.en: what is there? No one experiences anything.
cues.zh: 还有什么呢？没有人体验任何事物。

cues.en: It's like, is there anything when no one experiences anything? That's the question. And the answer that this book is presenting is that no, you have to think about consciousness as a constituent
cues.zh: 就像，如果没有人体验任何事物，还存在什么吗？这就是问题所在。而这本书给出的答案是：不，你必须把意识视为现实的一个构成

cues.en: element of reality. It's something that's necessary for reality
cues.zh: 要素。它是现实本身得以存在的必要之物

cues.en: itself to exist. Now of course it depends on what you mean by reality.
cues.zh: 。当然，这取决于你所说的现实是什么意思。

cues.en: But the reality that's being referred to here, I told you already, is this strange amalgam of the subjective experience and the world. But the question is deeper than that too because it is by no means obvious what there is if there's no one to experience it. Mean, the whole notion of time itself seems to collapse, at least in terms of something like felt duration.
cues.zh: 但这里所指的现实，我已经告诉过你了，是主观体验与世界的那种奇特的混合体。但这个问题比那更深，因为如果没有一个体验者，那里究竟有什么绝不是显而易见的。我的意思是，时间本身的整个概念似乎都崩解了，至少就类似被感受到的持续时间而言是这样。

cues.en: And the notion of size disappears essentially because there's nothing to scale it and the causality seems to vanish.
cues.zh: 而大小的概念基本消失了，因为没有什么能衡量它，因果关系似乎也消失了。

cues.en: And we don't understand consciousness,
cues.zh: 而我们不理解意识，

cues.en: not in the least.
cues.zh: 一点也不理解。

cues.en: We don't understand what it is that is in us that gives illumination to being. And what happens in the Old Testament, at least in part, is that that consciousness is associated
cues.zh: 我们不明白我们内在是什么赋予了存在以光明。而在《旧约》中发生的事情，至少部分上，是那种意识被关联

cues.en: with the divine.
cues.zh: 于神性。

cues.en: Now you think, well is that a reasonable proposition?
cues.zh: 现在你想，那是个合理的命题吗？

cues.en: And that's a very complicated question. But at least we might note that there's something to the claim.
cues.zh: 这是一个非常复杂的问题。但至少我们可以注意到，这个说法是有一定道理的。

cues.en: Because
cues.zh: 因为

cues.en: there is a miracle of experience and existence that's dependent on consciousness. I mean, people try to explain it away constantly, but it doesn't seem to work very well. And here's something else to think about,
cues.zh: 经验与存在有一个奇迹，它依赖于意识。我的意思是，人们总是试图把它解释掉，但这似乎并不太奏效。还有一点值得思考，

cues.en: I think, that's really worth thinking about. People do not like it when you treat them like they're not conscious.
cues.zh: 我认为，这点真的值得思考。当你不把人们当作有意识的存在来对待时，他们是不喜欢的。

cues.en: Right? They react very badly to that.
cues.zh: 对吧？他们对这个反应很强烈。

cues.en: And then you don't like it if someone assumes that you're not conscious, and you don't like it if someone assumes that you don't have free will. You know, that you're just absolutely determined in your actions
cues.zh: 然后你不喜欢别人假设你没有意识，也不喜欢别人假设你没有自由意志。你知道，就是说你的行为完全是注定的，

cues.en: and there's nothing that's going to repair you and that you don't need to have any responsibility for your actions. It's like, our culture, the laws of our culture are predicated on the idea, something like people are conscious, people have experience, people make decisions and can be held responsible for them, that there's a free will element to it. And you can debate all that philosophically,
cues.zh: 没有什么能修复你，你不需要为自己的行为承担任何责任。就像我们的文化，我们文化的法律是建立在这个观念之上的：人有意识、人有体验、人能做出决定并为之负责，其中有自由意志的成分。你可以在哲学上争论这一切，

cues.en: and fine. But the point is that
cues.zh: 那没问题。但关键是，

cues.en: that is how we act and that is the idea that our legal system is predicated on. And there's something deep about it because,
cues.zh: 这就是我们的行为方式，也是我们法律体系所依据的观念。这其中有很深的东西，因为，

cues.en: you know,
cues.zh: 你知道，

cues.en: you're subject to the law,
cues.zh: 你受法律约束，

cues.en: but the law is also limited by you. Which is to say that in in a well functioning,
cues.zh: 但法律也受你限制。也就是说，在一个运作良好、

cues.en: properly grounded democratic system,
cues.zh: 根基正当的民主制度中，

cues.en: you have
cues.zh: 你拥有

cues.en: intrinsic
cues.zh: 内在的

cues.en: value.
cues.zh: 价值。

cues.en: That's the source of your rights.
cues.zh: 这就是你权利的来源。

cues.en: Even if you're a murderer,
cues.zh: 即使你是个杀人犯，

cues.en: we have to say the law can only go so far because there's something about you that's divine.
cues.zh: 我们也得说法律只能到此为止，因为你身上有某种神圣的东西。

cues.en: Well, what does that mean? Well, partly it means that there's something about you that's conscious and capable of communicating, like you're a whole world unto yourself.
cues.zh: 那是什么意思呢？部分意思是，你身上有某种有意识、能沟通的东西，就像你本身就是一个完整的世界。

cues.en: And you have that to contribute to everyone else, and that's valuable. You
cues.zh: 你能把这贡献给其他人，这很有价值。你

cues.en: can learn new things, you can transform the structure of society, you can invent a new way of dealing with the world. You're capable of all that. It's an intrinsic part of you, and that's associated with this.
cues.zh: 能学新东西，能改变社会结构，能发明应对世界的新方式。这些你都做得到。这是你内在的一部分，与此相关。

cues.en: It's associated... That's the idea there, is that there's something about the logos
cues.zh: 它相关……这就是那个理念：道（logos）有某种东西

cues.en: that is necessary for the absolute chaos of the reality beyond experience to manifest itself as reality.
cues.zh: 是让超越经验的现实的绝对混沌显现为现实所必需的。

cues.en: It's an amazing idea because it gives consciousness
cues.zh: 这是个了不起的想法，因为它赋予意识

cues.en: a constitutive
cues.zh: 一种构成性

cues.en: role in the cosmos.
cues.zh: 的角色，在宇宙之中。

cues.en: And you can debate that, but you know, it's not... You can't just bloody well brush it off.
cues.zh: 你可以对此争论，但你知道，这不是……你不能就这么轻率地把它打发掉。

cues.en: Because first of all, we are the most complicated things there are that we know of by
cues.zh: 因为首先，我们是我们所知的最复杂的东西，

cues.en: a massive amount. We're so complicated that it's unbelievable.
cues.zh: 而且复杂程度远超其他，差距巨大。我们复杂得令人难以置信。

cues.en: And so, you know, there's a lot of cosmos out there, but there's a lot of cosmos in here too. And which one is greater is by no means obvious, unless you use something trivial like relative size, which really isn't a very sophisticated approach.
cues.zh: 所以，你知道，外面有浩瀚的宇宙，但这里也有浩瀚的宇宙。哪一个更宏大，绝非显而易见，除非你用相对大小这种琐碎的标准，而那真不是一种很成熟的做法。

cues.en: And whatever it is that is you has this capacity
cues.zh: 而无论“你”是什么，都具有这种能力

cues.en: to experience reality and to transform it, which is a very strange thing, you know. You can conceptualize a future in your imagination.
cues.zh: 去体验现实并改变现实，这非常奇妙。你能在想象中构想未来。

cues.en: And then you can work and make that manifest.
cues.zh: 然后你可以付诸行动，让它成为现实。

cues.en: You participate in the process of creation.
cues.zh: 你参与了创造的过程。

cues.en: That's one way of thinking about it. And so that's why I think in Genesis
cues.zh: 这是一种理解方式。所以我认为在《创世记》中

cues.en: one,
cues.zh: 第一，

cues.en: it relates
cues.zh: 它讲述了

cues.en: the idea that human beings are made in the image of the divine, men and women, which is interesting too because, you know, the feminists
cues.zh: 人类是按照神的形象创造的，男人和女人都是，这也很有意思，因为你知道，女权主义者

cues.en: are always criticizing Christianity,
cues.zh: 总是批评基督教，

cues.en: for example, as being, what, inexorably
cues.zh: 比如说，说它是不可救药的

cues.en: patriarchal.
cues.zh: 父权制。

cues.en: Or they criticize everything like that, so it's hardly a stroke of bloody brilliance.
cues.zh: 或者他们那样批评一切，所以这算不上什么血腥的天才之举。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: I think it's an absolute miracle that right at the beginning of the document it says straightforwardly,
cues.zh: 我觉得这绝对是个奇迹，就在文件的开头，它直截了当地说，

cues.en: with no hesitation whatsoever, that the divine spark, which we're associating with the word that brings forth being, is manifest in men and women equally. That's a very cool thing. And you've got to think, well, like I said, you actually take that seriously. Well, what you've to ask is, what happens if you don't take it seriously?
cues.zh: 毫不犹豫地说，我们与引出存在的词相关联的神圣火花，在男女中平等显现。这非常酷。你得想想，嗯，就像我说的，你实际上认真对待这一点。那么，你要问的是，如果你不认真对待会怎样？

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: Read Dostoevsky's
cues.zh: 去读陀思妥耶夫斯基的

cues.en: Crime and Punishment.
cues.zh: 《罪与罚》。

cues.en: That's the best
cues.zh: 那是对

cues.en: investigation
cues.zh: 那种策略

cues.en: of that
cues.zh: 最精彩的

cues.en: tactic that's ever been produced. Because what happens in
cues.zh: 剖析，前所未有。因为

cues.en: Dostoevsky's
cues.zh: 在陀思妥耶夫斯基的

cues.en: Crime and Punishment is that the main character, whose name is Raskolnikov,
cues.zh: 《罪与罚》里，主角拉斯柯尔尼科夫

cues.en: decides that there's no intrinsic value to other people.
cues.zh: 认定别人没有内在价值。

cues.en: And that as a consequence, he can do whatever he wants. It's only cowardice that stops him from acting.
cues.zh: 因此，他想做什么都可以。阻止他行动的只有懦弱。

cues.en: Right? Because
cues.zh: 对吧？因为

cues.en: why would it be anything else if
cues.zh: 如果别人的价值只是一种随意的迷信，

cues.en: the value of other people is just an arbitrary superstition?
cues.zh: 那还能有什么别的解释呢？

cues.en: Then why can't I do exactly what I want when I want? Which is the psychopath's viewpoint.
cues.zh: 那为什么我不能随心所欲、想做什么就做什么？这正是精神变态者的观点。

cues.en: Well, so Ryskolnikov does. He kills someone who's a very horrible person, and he has very good reasons for killing her. And he's half starved and a little bit insane and possessed by this ideology. It's brilliant, brilliant layout.
cues.zh: 嗯，拉斯柯尔尼科夫就是这么做的。他杀了一个非常可怕的人，而且他有充分的理由杀她。他半饥半饱，有点疯癫，还被这种意识形态所支配。这构思真是精妙绝伦。

cues.en: And he finds out something after he kills her, which is that the post killing Ryskolnikov
cues.zh: 而在杀她之后，他发现了一件事：杀人之后的拉斯柯尔尼科夫

cues.en: and the pre killing Ryskolnikov
cues.zh: 和杀人之前的拉斯柯尔尼科夫

cues.en: are not the same person, even a little bit. He's broken a rule. He's broken a serious rule and there's no going back. And crime and punishment is
cues.zh: 根本不是同一个人，一点都不一样。他打破了一条规则。他打破了一条严重的规则，而且再也回不去了。而《罪与罚》是

cues.en: the best investigation I know of, of what happens if you take the notion that there's nothing divine about the individual seriously.
cues.zh: 我所知道的最好的探究——探究如果你当真认为个体身上没有任何神圣之处，会发生什么。

cues.en: Now you
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: know,
cues.zh: 你知道，

cues.en: most of the people I know who are deeply atheistic, and understand why they're deeply atheistic, they haven't contended with people like Dostoevsky.
cues.zh: 我认识的大多数坚定无神论者，以及理解他们为何坚定无神论的人，都没有与像陀思妥耶夫斯基这样的人较量过。

cues.en: Not as far as I can tell. Because I don't see logical flaws in Crime and Punishment. I think he got the psychology exactly right. And Dostoevsky's
cues.zh: 据我所知没有。因为我在《罪与罚》中看不到逻辑缺陷。我认为他把心理刻画得完全准确。而陀思妥耶夫斯基

cues.en: amazing for this because in one of his books, The Devils, for example,
cues.zh: 在这方面很了不起，因为在他的一本书《群魔》中，举例来说，

cues.en: he describes a political
cues.zh: 他描述了一个政治

cues.en: scenario that's not much different than the one we find ourselves in now. And there are these people who are possessed by rationalistic,
cues.zh: 场景，与我们现在的处境相差无几。有一些人被理性主义的、

cues.en: utopian, atheistic ideas,
cues.zh: 乌托邦式的、无神论的思想所支配，

cues.en: and they're very powerful. They give rise to the communist revolution, right? I mean, they're powerful ideas. And his character,
cues.zh: 他们非常强大。他们催生了共产主义革命，对吧？我是说，这些思想很有力量。而他的角色，

cues.en: Stavragan,
cues.zh: 斯塔夫罗金，

cues.en: also acts out the
cues.zh: 也演绎了

cues.en: presupposition that human beings have no intrinsic nature and no intrinsic value.
cues.zh: 这样一个预设：人类没有内在本质，也没有内在价值。

cues.en: And it's another brilliant investigation,
cues.zh: 又是一次精彩的探究，

cues.en: Dostoevsky
cues.zh: 陀思妥耶夫斯基

cues.en: prophesies, that's what I would say, what will happen to a society if it goes down that road. And he was dead exactly
cues.zh: 预言了，我想说，一个社会如果走上那条路会发生什么。而他的预言完全

cues.en: accurate. It's uncanny to read Dostoevsky's
cues.zh: 准确。读陀思妥耶夫斯基的

cues.en: The Possessed or The Devil's, depending on the translation, and then to read Alexander Solzhenitsyn's Gulag Archipelago.
cues.zh: 《群魔》——看译本也叫《魔鬼》——然后再读亚历山大·索尔仁尼琴的《古拉格群岛》，那种感觉真是诡异。

cues.en: Because one is fiction and prophecy,
cues.zh: 因为一个是小说和预言，

cues.en: and the second is, hey, look, it turned out exactly the way that Dostoevsky said it would for exactly the same reasons.
cues.zh: 另一个则是：嘿，你看，事情恰恰按照陀思妥耶夫斯基所说的方式发生了，原因也完全相同。

cues.en: So it's quite remarkable.
cues.zh: 这非常了不起。

cues.en: Well, so the question is, do you contend seriously with the idea that a) there's something
cues.zh: 那么问题在于，你是否认真思考过这样一种观点：a) 存在某种

cues.en: cosmically constitutive
cues.zh: 在宇宙层面具有构成性意义的

cues.en: about consciousness,
cues.zh: 意识，

cues.en: and b) that
cues.zh: b) 它

cues.en: that might well be considered divine, and c) that that is instantiated in every person? And then ask yourself if you're not a criminal
cues.zh: 很可能被视为神圣的，以及 c) 它在每个人身上都有体现？然后问问自己，如果你不将其付诸行动，

cues.en: if you don't act it out. And then ask yourself what that means. Is that reflective of a reality?
cues.zh: 你是否就是个罪人。然后问问自己这意味着什么。这反映了某种现实吗？

cues.en: Is it a metaphor? Like maybe it's a metaphor, a complex metaphor that we have to use to organize our societies. Could well be, but
cues.zh: 这是一个隐喻吗？也许它就是个隐喻，一个我们不得不用来组织社会的复杂隐喻。很有可能，但

cues.zh: 它必须是某种东西的工具。

cues.en: And what the humanities were for was to tell people what the tools should be used for. And so the tools themselves are crazily powerful. But that's not necessarily
cues.zh: 而人文学科的作用就是告诉人们这些工具应该用来做什么。所以工具本身强大得离谱。但那未必

cues.en: an untrammeled good.

cues.en: K. You were in this, I guess, one room in a museum in New York where you'd seen some original Renaissance artwork masterpieces.
cues.zh: 好。你当时在，我猜，纽约某博物馆的一个房间里，看过一些文艺复兴时期的原作杰作。

cues.en: Yep. These are generally accepted as amazing
cues.zh: 是的。这些普遍被认为是了不起的

cues.en: artifacts. Okay?
cues.zh: 艺术品。对吧？

cues.en: Does an original work of art as opposed to a high fidelity reproduction
cues.zh: 一件原作，相对于高保真复制品，

cues.en: contain the spirit of the artist who created it, and does this account for the disparity in how much you'd have to pay for an original? It does in part. I knew a good portrait artist, and
cues.zh: 是否包含创作者的精神，这是否解释了原作为什么要贵那么多？部分上是。我认识一位优秀的肖像画家，而且

cues.en: one of the things he pointed out about a great portrait is that it actually contains time.
cues.zh: 他指出过一件伟大肖像画的特点之一：它实际上蕴含着时间。

cues.en: So, you know, because a photograph is one instant.
cues.zh: 所以，你知道，因为照片只是一个瞬间。

cues.en: But a portrait is you layered on you, layered on you, so it's got a thickness.
cues.zh: 但肖像画是你叠在你之上，再叠在你之上，所以它有厚度。

cues.en: You know, and I think you can see that thickness in the original, but it's also a direct manifestation of that creative act of perception.
cues.zh: 你知道，我觉得你能在原作中看到那种厚度，但它也是那种创造性感知行为的直接体现。

cues.en: And I don't think you get that. You just can't get the fidelity
cues.zh: 而且我不认为你能得到那种东西。你根本无法通过复制品获得原作的保真度。

cues.en: of the original with the reproduction. But there's more to it than that too because the painting doesn't end with the frame. We tend to think of the painting itself as the object, but most
cues.zh: 但事情还不止于此，因为画作并不止于画框。我们倾向于把画作本身当作对象，但大多数

cues.en: objects are densely
cues.zh: 对象都密布着

cues.en: innervated with historical
cues.zh: 历史的

cues.en: context.
cues.zh: 语境。

cues.en: And you can say, well, the historical context isn't the object, but it depends on what you mean by the object. And often people, when they buy a painting,
cues.zh: 你可以说，历史背景并不是对象本身，但这取决于你怎么定义对象。通常人们买一幅画的时候，

cues.en: are buying the historical context, and you just don't get that with the reproduction. It's a kind of magic. It's like, do you wanna have Elvis Presley's guitar or another guitar just like it?
cues.zh: 买的正是它的历史背景，而复制品根本无法给你这些。这有点像魔法。就好比，你是想要猫王用过的吉他，还是另一把一模一样的吉他？

cues.en: Well, you wanna have Elvis's guitar. It's why. You can't tell it's Elvis's guitar by looking at it.
cues.zh: 你肯定想要猫王那把。原因就在这儿。可你光看外观，根本分辨不出哪把是猫王的吉他。

cues.en: Well, it is at the level of detail, but not at the level of context. That's how it looks to me. Okay, we gotta go.
